title: Inconsistency of supersymmetric dimensional regularization
claim: Shows that DRED as proposed in S2.01 is mathematically inconsistent and outlines what must be changed for a consistent version.
scheme: DRED with 4-dimensional gamma matrices / epsilon tensors and a d-dimensional (d<4) momentum space embedded in the 4-dimensional index space.
symmetry_argument: Not a symmetry argument: an algebraic contradiction. As reported in S2.10 (Sec. 1): combining 4-dimensional gamma matrices and epsilon tensors with a d-dimensional metric yields 0 = d(d-1)(d-2)(d-3)(d-4); the trigger is the projector relation g^{mu nu} ghat_nu^rho = ghat^{mu rho} (eq. 4 of S2.10) used together with genuinely 4-dimensional epsilon/metric identities. S2.09 (Sec. 3, eqs. 15-19) phrases it as contradictions such as (d+1)(d-2) epsilonhat^{mu nu} = 0 obtained by evaluating epsilon-epsilon contractions in different orders.

proved: The combination 'd-dimensional momenta inside a strictly 4-dimensional index space with all 4-dimensional identities available' is contradictory for non-integer d.

evidence: INSPIRE abstract: scheme mathematically inconsistent; required modifications outlined.
S2.10 hep-ph/0503129 Sec. 1-2: the identity 0 = D(D-1)(D-2)(D-3)(D-4) (unnumbered), eqs. (3)-(4) of that paper identify the ingredients.
red_flags: The contradiction implies that a consistent DRED must forbid purely 4-dimensional identities (index counting, 5-index antisymmetrisation, Fierz rearrangements, epsilon-tensor products) inside d-dimensional expressions; but the classical SUSY invariance of the action uses Fierz identities, so a consistent DRED can break SUSY (made explicit in S2.10).
cross_checks: S2.09_JackJones1997 (view that the problem is technical and avoidable for physical results)
source_access: secondary: cited in hep-ph/0503129 (Sec. 1-2) and hep-ph/9707278 (Sec. 3); INSPIRE abstract
notes: Original text not accessed; the explicit identity is quoted from the two secondary sources, which present it in different but equivalent forms.
